name: Borneo-eiland
wikipediaExtract: Borneo-eiland is a peninsula in Amsterdam-Oost between the Spoorwegbassin and the Entrepothaven, in the former eastern docklands. It takes its name from the Borneokade, which was named in 1917 after the East Indian island of Borneo. It was a port and industrial area until the 1980s and was then redeveloped for housing. A rider will notice the Scheepstimmermanstraat, where 60 houses were designed by different architects, and two red bridges that link the island to Sporenburg.

name: KNSM-eiland
wikipediaExtract: KNSM-eiland is a peninsula in the IJ in Amsterdam, one of the neighbourhoods of the Oostelijk Havengebied. The island was extended eastward just before 1900 and is named after the Koninklijke Nederlandse Stoomboot-Maatschappij, the shipping company that operated there from 1903 to 1979. Its large brick block Piraeus (1994, Hans Kollhoff) and the residential tower Skydome (1996, Wiel Arets) are the standout buildings, and a warehouse, a harbour crane and a canteen building survive as municipal monuments.

name: Oostelijk Havengebied
wikipediaExtract: The Oostelijk Havengebied is the north-western neighbourhood of Amsterdam-Oost, facing the IJ. The municipality began creating its land in 1890 with a dam in the IJ, and from the mid-1980s the former port land was given a residential purpose and developed into a modern housing area in the 1990s. The Java and KNSM islands are largely built up with high-rise, while Borneo and Sporenburg have low and mid-rise housing, so the area has been called a who's who of recent architecture. Tram line 26, the IJtram, opened to IJburg in 2005.

name: Buitenveldert
wikipediaExtract: Buitenveldert is a neighbourhood in the south of Amsterdam, on the former Binnendijksche Buitenveldertse polder, which the city annexed in 1921. The 1935 General Expansion Plan made the polder the site of a new suburb, planned on garden-city principles; the first stone was laid in 1958 and the first residents moved in in 1959. The Kalfjeslaan on its south side has been the city limit since then, and the Gelderlandplein shopping centre is the highlight of the residential area. It is also considered the modern Jewish quarter of Amsterdam.

name: IJburg
wikipediaExtract: IJburg is a residential neighbourhood in Amsterdam's Oost borough, built on artificial islands in the IJmeer. The municipality approved it in 1996, a 1997 referendum fell short of the vote threshold so construction could proceed, and the first residents moved into Rieteiland in spring 2008. The first phase consists of Steigereiland, Haveneiland and the Rieteilanden. Tram line 26 (the IJtram) runs along the IJburglaan to Central Station, and the Nescio Bridge for pedestrians and cyclists ends in a spiral cycle ramp.

name: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
wikipediaExtract: Nieuwmarkt is a square in the centre of Amsterdam between the Geldersekade and the Kloveniersburgwal, bordering the Zeedijk to the north and the Sint Antoniesbreestraat to the south. It came into being in 1614, when the water around the Sint Anthoniespoort was covered over, and it became a market square. At its centre stands the Waag, originally a 15th-century city gate. The Lastage, the area between the Geldersekade and Oudeschans next to it, lost many houses in 1975 to a metro tunnel, which sparked the Nieuwmarkt riots.

name: Overtoomse Sluis
wikipediaExtract: The Overtoomse Sluis (bridge no. 199) crosses the Kostverlorenvaart in Amsterdam-West. The lock beneath it was 144 metres long with a 127-metre chamber and was 7.75 metres wide. On 1 July 1942 it was replaced by the Schinkelsluis near the Nieuwe Meer. The old Overtoomse Buurt largely disappeared in the 1920s for the construction of the Surinameplein.

name: Prinses Irenebuurt e.o.
wikipediaExtract: The Prinses Irenebuurt is a neighbourhood in Amsterdam-Zuid, bounded on the north by the Zuider Amstelkanaal. It was built between 1954 and 1958 and is named after the Prinses Irenestraat, itself named in 1953 after Princess Irene, daughter of Queen Juliana; many streets are named after Dutch composers and Juliana's daughters. A rider will notice the Warnersblokken, four residential blocks of 1957 by Allert Warners with colourful facade panels, a rijksmonument since 2010.

name: Sluisbuurt
wikipediaExtract: Sluisbuurt is a new neighbourhood on Zeeburgereiland in Amsterdam-Oost, next to the Oranjesluizen it is named after. The municipality decided in November 2018 to build it, with about 5,500 homes and 32 residential towers averaging about 60 metres and reaching 125 metres at most. A central water basin is planned for water recreation.

name: Sportheldenbuurt
wikipediaExtract: The Sportheldenbuurt is a residential neighbourhood on Zeeburgereiland on the east side of Amsterdam. Pile driving began in July 2012 and the first self-built homes were finished in 2013 and 2014. In 2011 the city announced that the streets would be named after figures from Dutch sports history, and the bridges on the outer edge were named likewise in 2016. Three large silos of the former sewage treatment plant were kept, and there is a marina.

name: VU-kwartier
wikipediaExtract: The VU-kwartier is the campus area of the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, one of five buurten of the statistical district Zuidas. The university moved there from the city centre from 1968 onwards, into the Buitenveldert neighbourhood, and its main campus along De Boelelaan now sits next to the Zuidas business district. The Main Building, established in 1973, stands at the corner of the Boelelaan and the Buitenveldertselaan.

name: Valkenburg
wikipediaExtract: Valkenburg, also known as Marken, is a former island in Amsterdam bounded by the Rapenburgwal, the Uilenburgergracht, the Markenplein and the Rapenburgerstraat. It was built up in the sixteenth century, one of three islands (Uilenburg, Valkenburg and Rapenburg) made by digging out land outside the dike, and before and during the Second World War it was part of the Jewish quarter. It stopped being an island after the redesign for the IJ-tunnel; today it holds a parking garage, the Markenhoven apartments and the Nederlandse Filmacademie.

name: Gouden Bocht
wikipediaExtract: The Gouden Bocht is the most prestigious stretch of the grandest canal of the ring, between the Leidsestraat and the Vijzelstraat, part of the Vierde Uitleg, the last extension of the canal belt. At the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat the canal takes a bend and the canals lie further apart, making the plots deeper; the mayors encouraged the purchase of double plots, where the city's richest residents built grand houses. Huis de Neufville (1731, at number 475) is often called the finest house on the bend, and today the offices of banks and insurers share it with the Goethe-Institut and the Kattenkabinet.
